**Manuscript Location:** {{< meta manuscript-location >}}  

Dear [Mr Wodehouse](../persons.html#1548)
I shall be delighted to see another story of [Miss Gordon](../persons.html#569)’s.[^2] I am in hopes that her icelandic one will appear in the [Packet](../others.html#52) in February or March, and indeed I was thinking of writing to ask where she was that I might send her the proofs, it is indeed a long time since we have met, and as my [brother](../persons.html#1624) and [sister](../persons.html#1604) have gone out and left us their cavalry, we are meditating driving to Easton some day, when we might bring home the MS.

Would you or [Lady Elinor](../persons.html#1547) be so kind as to let us know whether we should find you at home if we presented ourselves at luncheon the first fine day next week?

Yours very truly

C M Yonge

[^1]: Black-edged paper.

[^2]: Mary Charlotte Julia Gordon (1840-1926), later (1865) Mrs Disney Leith, was a niece of Lady Elinor Wodehouse, who was sister to her mother and to the mother of Algernon Swinburne, with whom Mary Gordon collaborated on a story The Children of the Chapel (1864).
